name: buzz
one_liner: A self-hosted team chat (like Slack) built from the ground up so AI agents can be first-class members of the conversation alongside humans, on a server you control.
buyer: A tech-forward engineering team that already leans on multiple AI agents for work and wants them embedded in team chat instead of bolted on as a bot.
business_use_cases: An engineering team self-hosts it so agents post status updates, ask clarifying questions, and get approvals in the same channel as humans.
A privacy-sensitive company (defense, finance, healthcare) runs it instead of Slack+Copilot to keep all agent-human chat on infrastructure it owns.
A dev tools startup offers managed hosting of it as the 'team layer' for companies rolling out AI agents at scale.

money_ideas.idea: Managed hosting with SSO, backups, and support, billed per workspace
Paid integration work connecting it to a company's specific internal agents and tools

steal_this: It's early and developer-facing — the realistic weekend build is a managed-hosting offering ('Buzz, but we run it for you') aimed at teams who want agent-aware chat without standing up Rust infrastructure themselves.
